name: Wildcat Ridge (delta front)
why: Mudstone at the foot of the river delta, laid down as the lake dried. Its samples (sealed sols 509 and 516) hold organic molecules detected by the rover's SHERLOC instrument
source: NASA/JPL M20 waypoint feed: rover stop at sol 502, the nearest to sol 509 (Hazeltop sample sealed, Wildcat Ridge)

name: Three Forks Sample Depot
why: The first sample depot on another planet: ten sealed tubes left on the ground (first dropped sol 653, Dec 2022) as a backup for Mars Sample Return. A crew could collect them on foot
source: NASA/JPL M20 waypoint feed: rover stop at sol 652, the nearest to sol 653 (first tube dropped at the depot)

name: Cheyava Falls (Neretva Vallis)
why: The 'leopard spot' rock NASA calls a potential biosignature: the Sapphire Canyon sample, sealed sol 1215, is the strongest candidate for ancient microbial life found so far
source: NASA/JPL M20 waypoint feed: rover stop at sol 1219, the nearest to sol 1215 (Sapphire Canyon sample sealed)

name: Silver Mountain (crater rim)
why: Perseverance's first sample from Jezero's rim (sealed sol 1401): ancient crust lifted up by the impact that made the crater, possibly among the oldest rock sampled on Mars
source: NASA/JPL M20 waypoint feed: rover stop at sol 1400, the nearest to sol 1401 (Silver Mountain sample sealed, Shallow Bay)
